pass2.systemImpact: CADRegressionSafetyHooks abort a CAD regression run on cascading failure — they protect the host (a 20K-file run that's failing every file wastes hours and memory) and prevent a corrupt run from feeding CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine (U-CINF10) a meaningless aggregate. If the abort gate doesn't fire, a cascade runs to completion and the dashboard reports a falsely-low pass-rate as if it were real signal.
csDepth: The circuit-breaker needs a failure-rate window, not a raw count — abort on 'N failures in the last M files', because an absolute count would never abort a long run with a steady low failure rate while a true cascade should trip fast; tune the window against real failure-burst data.

curatedWiki.buildNote: Voxel stock integration subtracts the swept tool volume per move — verify removed-material volume against analytical MRR; voxel resolution must be fine enough to not miss thin cuts.

A too-coarse voxel grid misses thin cuts, so the stock model diverges from reality and engagement/force estimates downstream are wrong.
csDepth: Voxel material-removal is a 3D occupancy-grid update — boolean subtraction of the swept tool volume per move; the grid resolution must be fine enough that no machined feature is thinner than a voxel, or thin cuts are silently missed (memory cost is O(n^3) in resolution — a real space/accuracy tradeoff).

csKnowledge: finite-difference gradient of an output w.r.t. each input

curatedWiki.buildNote: Sensitivity analysis at every decision must perturb each input and report the gradient — verify finite-difference sensitivity against an analytic case.

pass2.systemImpact: Sensitivity analysis at every decision reports how each input drives the decision output — it feeds the decision-explanation engine (U-CAMX08) and tells operators which input to control. A wrong sensitivity misdirects process-improvement effort.
csDepth: Finite-difference (one-at-a-time) sensitivity must pick a perturbation step that balances truncation error (too large) against floating-point cancellation (too small) — a fixed step can be wrong for inputs of very different magnitudes; scale the step to the input.

Local OAT sensitivity ignores interaction effects; for a decision with interacting inputs the per-input gradient understates total influence — note this limitation and prefer Sobol (U-CAMX06) where interactions matter.

csKnowledge: bidirectional sync with conflict detection (tool-library diff/merge)
idempotent sync (re-run produces no spurious changes)
orchestration over multiple per-vendor export engines
curatedWiki.buildNote: ToolSyncOrchestratorEngine must be idempotent and detect conflicts before writing — a re-sync of unchanged data must produce zero diffs.

pass2.systemImpact: ToolSyncOrchestratorEngine performs bidirectional tool-library sync across the per-vendor export engines — it keeps PRISM's tool model and external CAM tool libraries consistent. A non-idempotent sync produces spurious diffs on every re-run, and a missed conflict silently overwrites a vendor-side edit.
csDepth: Idempotent sync requires a stable diff: re-syncing unchanged data must produce zero diffs — this needs canonical serialization (stable field order, fixed precision) so identical data hashes identically.

Bidirectional sync must detect conflicts (both sides changed since last sync) before writing — a last-writer-wins merge silently discards one side's edit; conflict detection needs a per-record last-synced baseline.

pass3.topRecommendation: Read knowledge/wiki/architecture/engines/cam/camtoollibraryengine.md first — it is the closest existing engine; mind the build-note constraint: ToolSyncOrchestratorEngine must be idempotent and detect conflicts before writing — a re-sync of unchanged data must produce zero diffs.
